<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>README · Anchored Returns</title><link rel="stylesheet" href="/presentation/styles.css"></head><body class="document-page"><header class="document-header"><a href="/presentation/index.html">← Anchored Returns</a><span>Kazi Rafsan Mahboob · Research documents</span></header><main class="document-content"><h1>EEI historical electric benchmarks</h1><p>This collection reconstructs a separate national electric comparison series from the public <a href="https://www.eei.org/issues-and-policy/finance-and-tax" rel="noopener noreferrer">EEI Finance and Accounting resource library</a>. The source is the <strong>2025 Q3 Rate Review</strong> workbook, retrieved October 20, 2026. Its reporting date is September 30, 2025. The publication date has not been verified.</p><p>The workbook contains 2,589 observations in <code>All Rate Cases 2025Q3</code>, including 2,535 completed observations and 54 pending observations. The original sheet is hidden in the publicly distributed workbook. No credentials or access restriction were required to retrieve it. Three completed observations have authorization dates after its stated reporting date. These are flagged in the reconstruction report and do not enter any reported complete half-year.</p><h2>Files</h2><div class="doc-table"><table><thead><tr><th>File</th><th>Contents</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>eei_rate_review_2025_q3.xlsx</code></td><td>Original source bytes</td></tr><tr><td><code>source.json</code></td><td>URL, source vintage, retrieval date and SHA-256</td></tr><tr><td><code>electric_observations.csv</code></td><td>Every original observation, with sheet and row references</td></tr><tr><td><code>half_year_benchmarks.csv</code></td><td>Complete half-year means, denominators and row references</td></tr><tr><td><code>reconstruction.json</code></td><td>Benchmark records and 31 quarterly reconciliation checks</td></tr></tbody></table></div><h2>Calculation</h2><p>The comparison series uses completed electric observations classified as <code>Distribution</code> or <code>Vertically Integrated</code>. It excludes <code>Limited-Issue Rider</code> and <code>Transmission</code> observations. The workbook&#x27;s status <code>Settled</code> means that a case has a completed authorization entry. It is not a classification of negotiated versus litigated outcomes.</p><p>Each observation with a reported positive ROE receives equal weight. Missing ROEs remain missing and do not enter the denominator. The mean equals the sum of the individual ROE percentages divided by the number of observed ROEs. Two-decimal display values use decimal rounding with ties rounded upward. Exact sums, counts and unrounded means are retained. Two-decimal source ROEs are normalized only to remove Excel serialization differences smaller than 0.0000000001 percentage points.</p><p>The reconstruction also retains an all-case series for sensitivity comparisons. The source&#x27;s quarterly counts and averages are reproduced for all 31 quarters from 2018 Q1 through 2025 Q3. These checks use the workbook&#x27;s separate <code>Summary</code> sheet.</p><div class="doc-table"><table><thead><tr><th>Period</th><th>Base-rate decisions with ROE</th><th>Sum of ROE percentages</th><th>Mean ROE</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>2018 H2</td><td>19</td><td>181.35</td><td>9.54%</td></tr><tr><td>2023 H1</td><td>12</td><td>115.70</td><td>9.64%</td></tr><tr><td>2023 H2</td><td>36</td><td>347.88</td><td>9.66%</td></tr><tr><td>2024 H2</td><td>27</td><td>265.32</td><td>9.83%</td></tr><tr><td>2025 H1</td><td>18</td><td>174.23</td><td>9.68%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><h2>Interpretation</h2><p>These are retrospective EEI workbook reconstructions. They remain separate from the historical RRA original-report series. The current workbook may incorporate revisions and does not establish which observations were available on an earlier commission decision date. It contains electric observations only. It provides no gas comparison and no complete 2026 half-year.</p><p>The 2023 annual source table has 91 completed observations and 63 reported ROEs. Their case-weighted mean rounds to 9.60%, or 9.66% for the 48 base-rate observations with ROEs. The corresponding 2024 figures are 78 completed observations, 55 reported ROEs, a 9.74% all-case mean and a 9.78% mean for 41 base-rate observations with ROEs. These totals agree with the respective original RRA annual-report control values. Agreement of these aggregates does not prove identical historical coverage for every observation.</p><p>EEI&#x27;s annual Financial Review headlines report 9.58% for 2023 and 9.73% for 2024. The unweighted average of each year&#x27;s four quarterly workbook means rounds to those figures. This is an arithmetic reconciliation, not a confirmed statement of EEI&#x27;s annual headline calculation. Its annual chart footnote describes returns as equal-weighted without specifying the aggregation used for the annual headline. The half-year series here always weights individual observations equally.</p><h2>Reproduction</h2><pre><code>from src.eei_benchmarks import eei_report

report = eei_report(&quot;.&quot;)
assert all(check[&quot;status&quot;] == &quot;passed&quot; for check in report[&quot;controls&quot;])</code></pre><p>The parser uses Python&#x27;s standard library, checks the original file fingerprint, reads cached source values and never executes formulas or macros. Each benchmark includes the original worksheet row numbers that enter its calculation. An optional candidate list produces same-service, previous-half-year joins with explicit retrospective status.</p><p>Original publication rights remain with EEI and the underlying data owners. This collection does not assert a new license over their workbook.</p></main></body></html>
